flags.title: Submitted tokens are not valid ASINs
flags.detail: B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3 and B00hJ57DV are each 9 characters. The ASIN identifier is 10 characters (Amazon defines it as 'the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products', S24), so none of the three can address a catalog record as written. Each is alphanumeric, so only the length fails. A control run on 2026-11-14 settles what that means: passing a VALID 10-character ASIN to the same link.amazon short-link service returns the identical 404 page as an unknown code (E-11, source S36), so the service does not accept or truncate ASINs at all. The supplied codes are opaque short-link identifiers native to that service, and their resemblance to a truncated ASIN is a coincidence of appearance. No missing character was ever guessed, and none is recoverable. See F-28, which records the control and withdraws the earlier 'consistent with a truncation' wording.
flags.impact: Product identity, and every dependent field (title, brand, category, price, rating, commission band, competition), is unavailable.
flags.action_required: Re-supply the full 10-character ASIN or the complete amazon.<tld>/dp/<ASIN> URL for each item.

flags.title: Canonical product pages return Page Not Found
flags.detail: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B04G1MEwY , /dp/B02NbDxp3 and /dp/B00hJ57DV each returned Amazon's "Sorry! We couldn't find that page" error page when fetched on 2026-11-13.
flags.impact: Confirms the tokens do not exist in the catalog rather than merely being unresolvable from this network.
flags.action_required: None - evidence record. Re-verify if the ASINs are ever corrected.

flags.title: The three link.amazon codes are honoured lookups, but no Amazon document binds a code to a product
flags.detail: FINAL READING (2026-11-14, session 4338f55e; supersedes the withdrawn 'arbitrary fallback' wording and the 'permanent per-link token' wording). What is verified: (a) each of the three supplied link.amazon URLs resolves, reproducibly, to ONE specific Amazon product page — B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH; (b) an UNKNOWN code on the same service (https://link.amazon/B00TEST12) returns a 404 page ('You've clicked on an invalid URL'), so the service looks the code up and the token IS honoured — the earlier claim that the token was ignored and the destination arbitrary is falsified; (c) plpRedirect=mhFallback is also emitted on ordinary valid /dp/ loads and so is not evidence of a fallback; (d) each link carries its own btn_ref=srctok-… token, which rotates over time while the destination does not. What is NOT verified: no public Amazon document describes the link.amazon/<code> format or binds a code to a product ASIN, so the binding is established by observed behaviour, not by documentation.
flags.impact: The three products can be named and marketed as the destinations the supplied links resolve to, which is what this site now publishes. They cannot be claimed as 'the products named in the brief' until the owner confirms the mapping in Associates Central.
flags.action_required: Owner: confirm in Associates Central that these three destinations are the items to market, and supply links carrying the Associates tag (F-24).

flags.title: link.amazon is not the documented public Associates short-link domain
flags.detail: The domain does resolve (it is served from Amazon CloudFront ranges), but it is not the public program's documented short-link domain used for Associates links; the public canonical product form is amazon.<tld>/dp/<ASIN> and program tooling provides its own link formats (S09). No Amazon help page surfaced in this review documents `link.amazon/<token>` as a publisher-facing link format.
flags.impact: Links of this shape cannot be relied on for tagging or attribution, and an untagged link earns nothing.
flags.action_required: Generate links from SiteStripe or the API in the tagged format required by the Participation Requirements (R-07).

flags.title: PA-API 5.0 is deprecated - the plan and most public tooling write-ups are stale
flags.detail: Amazon's legacy PA-API documentation URL now serves a deprecation notice: PA-API 5 calls return HTTP 403 with AccessDenied and instruct integrators to migrate to the Creators API. Amazon's own public Associates tools page (referenced in the site's source list) still describes the Product Advertising API as the programmatic option.
flags.impact: Any collector, tutorial, or dependency built against PA-API 5 will fail at runtime, not at build time. Architecture here targets the Creators API and degrades to a BLOCKED status rather than scraping.
flags.action_required: Register for Creators API access in Associates Central when the account exists (prerequisite: >=10 qualifying sales in the past 30 days, per Amazon's docs).

flags.title: Three compliance-control rows cited controls and files that do not exist; one misquoted current policy
flags.detail: Found in a line-by-line re-verification of the repository on 2026-11-14. (1) R-01 cited `site/compliance-inject.js` as the mechanism that renders the required disclosure - no such file exists anywhere in the repository; the disclosure is in fact emitted by the page renderers and enforced by tools/validate_data.py::check_disclosure plus the workflow's disclosure step. (2) R-11 cited `tools/validate_data.py::assert_no_amazon_marks` - no such function exists; the implemented function is `check_marks`. (3) R-02 cited `tools/generate_articles.py::lint_disclosure_proximity` and R-06 cited `::lint_claims` - neither function exists; both rules are enforced inside the single `lint()` function, and R-06's inline evidence marker is `<!--evidence:` (the data.js summary said 'inline evidence reference', which is right in substance but the function name was invented). (4) R-09 stated that email/SMS channels are 'absent from the schema' so a scheduler cannot target them - the current Program Policies expressly PERMIT Special Links in solicited (opt-in) email, SMS and direct messaging, so the rule text was stale against the policy page updated April 14, 2026.
flags.impact: The published compliance table claimed control coverage that did not exist for four rows. No fabricated product or price data was involved - this is a control-accuracy defect, not a data-invention defect - but a reader auditing 'is this enforced?' would have been given a wrong file or function name, and R-09 misstated a permission as a prohibition.
flags.action_required: Corrected, in two steps. Step 1 (session bbe4ca47): R-01 and R-11 were given the real functions and files (`tools/validate_data.py::check_marks`, the page renderers) and R-01's invented `site/compliance-inject.js` reference was removed. Step 2 (final integration, session 4338f55e, after change request DD-1 items 1-3 from session dd87f326): R-02 and R-06 now name `lint()` - the function that actually performs the checks - instead of the non-existent `lint_disclosure_proximity` and `lint_claims`; R-06's `expires_utc` enforcement, which had never been implemented, is implemented now and covered by tests/test_pipeline.py::test_expired_promotion_copy_is_removed_and_linted; and R-09's requirement text was rewritten to the policy as published (solicited/opt-in only, certification on request) while keeping the repository's stricter web-only channel default as a self-imposed control, labelled as such (published as flag F-25). All four rows now cite mechanisms that exist in the code. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-11-14 by session d3ce1c29: `check_marks` exists (tools/validate_data.py:190); `lint()` exists (tools/generate_articles.py:164) and is the function R-02 and R-06 now name; `expires_utc` is parsed and enforced (tools/generate_articles.py:56-113) and covered by tests/test_pipeline.py::test_expired_promotion_copy_is_removed_and_linted (tests/test_pipeline.py:177); R-01's remaining mention of `site/compliance-inject.js` is an in-line record of the correction, not a live citation; R-09 states the permission accurately and labels the web-only default as self-imposed. All four rows now cite mechanisms that exist. F-16 is closed.

flags.title: Root dashboard stated '3 Verified affiliate products' and '11 items flagged' while the ledger states 0 identified

The root product page's own heading was 'Product Catalog - verified from official Amazon pages', and the executive-summary paragraph said the products 'are identified and verified'. Meanwhile ledger/products.json marks all three submitted items status=UNVERIFIED with null title/brand/category, ledger/flags.json contains 15 flags (not 11), and F-03/F-12 record that the three destinations are fallback pages, not a mapping of the submitted tokens. flags.title: Emeril manufacturer page contradicts itself on functions/presets, so the published 'conflict' row named the wrong second source
flags.detail: The published spec row for the Emeril Lagasse 26QT (P-02, 'Cooking functions / presets') reads '24 per Amazon listing title; 25 per the manufacturer's spec tile'. Re-read on 2026-11-14, the manufacturer's own page carries THREE different numbers: the description text says '24 one-touch cooking presets', a specification tile says '25 Cooking Pre-sets', and a feature block headed '10-In-1 Versatility' lists ten functions. The Amazon listing title observed on the same day likewise says '24 cooking functions'. So the disagreement is not Amazon-vs-manufacturer - it is the manufacturer page disagreeing with itself, and no official source fixes the right number. Re-read again on 2026-11-14 by session 4338f55e with the same result: the Emeril Everyday page states '24 one-touch cooking presets' in its description, '25 Cooking Pre-sets' in its specification tile, and a feature block headed '10-In-1 Versatility' listing ten functions, while the Amazon listing title says '24 cooking functions'. The conflict is confirmed and remains unresolved.
flags.impact: The row was not wrong about a conflict existing, but it attributed the conflict to the wrong party, which would mislead a reader trying to resolve it. The value is unconfirmable, so it must stay blank-or-both-values and flagged rather than resolved by inference.
flags.action_required: Corrected: the row now shows all four observations with their exact source wording and status=conflict; flag F-19 published. Reviewer action: treat the preset count as unresolved; do not publish a single number in any article.

flags.title: DECISIVE CONTROL — an unknown link.amazon code returns a 404, so the three supplied codes are honoured lookups
flags.detail: Run 2026-11-14 by session 4338f55e, the control the earlier sessions did not run. GET https://link.amazon/B00TEST12 — a 9-character code that was never supplied — resolved to https://amzlinks.in/B00TEST12 and returned the short-link service's 404 page: '404: File Not Found … You've clicked on an invalid URL.' (the page's image is hosted at amzlinks.in/post-tap/short-link-404.png). The three supplied codes do not behave that way: each resolves to one specific Amazon product page, reproducibly, across fetches on 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14. A service that answered unknown codes with a random product would be a fallback; a service that answers unknown codes with a 404 is performing a lookup. Therefore the published reading that the token was 'ignored' and the destination 'arbitrary' is falsified.
flags.impact: This is the single finding that decides the disagreement between five earlier sessions. It moves the three products from 'evidence only' to 'the observed, reproducible destination of each supplied link' — while leaving the documentation gap (F-04, F-03) exactly as it was.
flags.action_required: None for the owner to unblock. Recorded so the reviewer can see the control and repeat it: open https://link.amazon/B00TEST12 in a browser.

flags.title: The link-rewrite token (btn_ref) rotates between days while the destination ASIN does not — so the token is not a usable identity marker
flags.detail: Measured 2026-11-14 by session 4338f55e. link.amazon/B04G1MEwY carried btn_ref=srctok-1e229870efde5acf earlier the same day (recorded by session c6e94e8d) and btn_ref=srctok-1f979f303a4b5691 at about 10:04 UTC, while the destination stayed /dp/B0CDY277D3 on every fetch. A direct, untagged load of /dp/B08DKYBTPH carries no btn_ref at all. The three supplied links' tokens are distinct from one another (1f979f303a4b5691 / 0cd8be3c7e2e0de3 / 7c59360cbbbd59b7) and all three carry channelId=704. Independent live re-fetch on 2026-11-14 by session a133aa61 recorded the same three destinations with different per-link tokens: link.amazon/B04G1MEwY carried btn_ref=srctok-1f979f303a4b5691 (earlier sessions recorded srctok-1e229870efde5acf), B02NbDxp3 carried srctok-0cd8be3c7e2e0de3 (earlier srctok-534f5e7952f396b2), and B00hJ57DV carried srctok-7c59360cbbbd59b7 (earlier srctok-76c3adaeb8708b44). Within a single day the token is stable; across days it is not.
flags.impact: Two published statements were each half-wrong: 'a different btn_ref on re-fetch proves the destination shuffles' (F-05, F-12 — withdrawn) and 'an identical btn_ref proves the token is permanent' (revalidation C-2 — overstated). The correct statement is that the source token is per-link and time-scoped, and the destination is stable. Anyone auditing this repository by re-fetching a link tomorrow should expect a different srctok and the same product. The ASIN, the page body and the channelId=704 parameter all reproduce across sessions and across days, so the destination findings stand; only the token's stability claim does not. Read btn_ref as evidence of a live redirect, never as an identifier.
flags.action_required: None — published so the wording is not misread as a guarantee of permanence in either direction. Do not use the btn_ref value as a stable identifier for anything. Confirm the three destinations in Associates Central and regenerate the links with the Associates tag.

flags.title: The Amazon title for B08DKYBTPH says '450°F Hi-Fry', but that same page's bullet list and specification block — and the manufacturer — say 200–400 °F
flags.detail: Verified 2026-11-14. The Amazon listing title for B08DKYBTPH reads 'Chefman Air Fryer 8 Qt | TurboFry® 4-in-1 with 450°F Hi-Fry Option for Crispier Results'. On the same page the 'About this item' bullet says 'a temperature range from 200-400°F' and the Product information block gives 'Min Temperature Setting: 94 °C' and 'Max Temperature Setting: 400 °F'. Chefman's own page for model RJ38-SQSS-8T states '200–400°F / 95º-205ºC' and 'Max temp: 400ºF/ 205ºC'. The Hi-Fry name and the 450 °F figure belong to the 6-quart dual-window model RJ38-SQPF-3TDB-2W, whose Chefman page states 'Max temp: 450ºF/ 235ºC with Hi-Fry function'.
flags.impact: Repeating '450 °F' in an article or comparison for the 8-quart model would repeat a claim the product's own specification block contradicts. 450 °F is publishable only for the 6-quart dual-window model.
flags.action_required: Copy rule published: no 450 °F claim for the 8-quart model. Owner action: none required.

flags.title: The three supplied links carry no Associates tag, so as supplied they cannot earn a commission
flags.detail: Verified 2026-11-14. Every resolved URL ends …&channelId=704&plpRedirect=mhFallback (short-link arrival) or …?lv=shuf&channelId=500&plpRedirect=mhFallback&th=1 (direct arrival); none carries a tag= parameter. Amazon's own help page gives the qualifying Special Link format as http://www.amazon.com/dp/ASIN/ref=nosim?tag=YOURASSOCIATEID and states that the tag identifies the Associates account the sale is tracked to.
flags.impact: As supplied, the three links would earn nothing and could not be attributed in reporting. This blocks revenue, not identification — it is the one step that turns this repository from a verified research platform into a earning affiliate site.
flags.action_required: Owner: supply the Associates ID (and the target marketplace) so links can be regenerated in the tagged format the program requires.

flags.title: Compliance row R-09 corrected: solicited email/SMS is permitted by the Program Policies, so the repo's web-only default is now labelled self-imposed
flags.detail: Re-read live on 2026-11-14. Participation Requirements (legacy page) Requirement 6 lists offline, email, SMS, MMS and print as examples of promotional activity that is not expressly permitted. Program Policies, Participation Requirements §4, states the same restriction and then expressly permits Special Links in emails, SMS and direct messaging from your social media Sites provided the communications are solicited (opted into by the recipient). An earlier revision of R-09 restated that permission as a flat prohibition.
flags.impact: No published claim depended on it, and the repository's control was already stricter than the policy. The row now states the requirement accurately and labels the web-only restriction as this project's own default.
flags.action_required: None. Optionally document an opt-in process before enabling an email/SMS channel.

flags.title: The dashboard's flag count was derived from the wrong list and understated the register (14 shown, 21 held)
flags.detail: F-17 (and the original F-22 on main, renumbered here to F-26) replaced a typed '11 items flagged' KPI with a derived count, which was the right direction. But the value was derived from FLAGGED_ROWS in assets/js/data.js - the reader-facing *subset* rendered on flagged.html - not from the canonical register in ledger/flags.json. As flags F-20 and F-21 were added to the register the dashboard kept showing 14 while pages/flags.html published 21, so one site told two different numbers. Only visible on the deployed page: no gate compared the JS constant to the ledger.
flags.impact: A KPI that understates the number of open items is a disclosure problem, not a cosmetic one: it tells the reader the site is cleaner than it is. It is the same class of defect as F-17.
flags.action_required: None open. CANONICAL_FLAG_COUNT now lives in assets/js/data.js and tools/validate_data.py::check_flag_count fails the build when it disagrees with the ledger (negative-tested: setting it to 14 turns the gate red).

flags.title: research-hub/scripts/build.py deletes its own output before every input is present, and cannot rebuild the hub from this tree
flags.detail: Running `python3 research-hub/scripts/build.py` (the hub's generator, not the root generators) deleted all 13 committed pages under research-hub/ and then aborted with FileNotFoundError on 'research-hub/docs/executive-summary.md'. Two faults combine: (a) it resolves its paths against the repository root instead of the hub directory, the same relocation defect repaired in research-hub/scripts/verify.py (I-27); and (b) it removes its previous output before it has read every input, so one missing input leaves the site with no pages. The pages were restored from git within the same session and every gate re-ran green, so nothing was published broken. The reference to 'docs/executive-summary.md' shows the hub's source document now lives outside the hub, so the generator cannot reproduce the published hub here even with correct paths.
flags.impact: A reader or a future automated session that runs this generator loses the entire research-hub/ site from the working tree. CI does not run it (0 references in .github/workflows/pages.yml), so the deployed site is unaffected, but the hazard is real and one command away.
flags.action_required: Do not run research-hub/scripts/build.py in this tree. The owning session should repoint it at the hub directory and make it verify its inputs before deleting output, or archive it beside the generated pages. Recorded rather than patched because research-hub/** is another session's namespace and its input layout has moved.

flags.title: The "one-character truncation" reading of the supplied 9-character codes is not supported
flags.detail: Evidence row E-05 recorded that each supplied code is 9 characters while an ASIN is 10, and offered the interpretation "Pattern is consistent with a one-character truncation". Session ba8b2d38 ran the control that tests it: passing a VALID 10-character ASIN (B0CDY277D3, which renders normally at amazon.com/dp/B0CDY277D3) to the same short-link service returns the identical 404 page as an unknown code (E-11, source S36). A service that accepted and truncated ASINs would resolve a correct one; this service does not accept ASINs at all. The 9-character codes are therefore opaque short-link identifiers, and their resemblance to a truncated ASIN is appearance only. Nothing else changes: the tokens are still not ASINs (F-01), no character was ever guessed, and the three destinations are unchanged. The interpretation in E-05 is marked corrected in place rather than deleted, so the record still shows what the site said and why. NOTE ON NUMBERING: this finding was first written up locally as F-27; when it was rebased onto main, session b38cc982 had already published a different F-27 (research-hub/scripts/build.py deletes its own output), so this one was renumbered to F-28 rather than overwrite theirs.
flags.impact: No published figure changes. It removes a plausible-sounding but unsupported explanation that a reader could otherwise use to assume the supplied links are simply mistyped ASINs and "obviously" refer to a recoverable product - which would invite exactly the guess this project refuses to make.
flags.action_required: None. Reproduce the control by opening https://link.amazon/B0CDY277D3 in a browser; compare with https://link.amazon/B00TEST12 (unknown code) and https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CDY277D3 (valid product).

flags.title: The bounty table published 9 of the 46 bounty events, and none of the 2 bonus events, under a 'transcribed row-by-row' notice
flags.detail: Found 2026-11-14 by session d3ce1c29. pages/commissions.html carried a panel headed 'Bounty events (Special Commission Income)' with nine rows, introduced by the notice 'Transcribed row-by-row from Amazon's published Associates Program Standard Commission Income Statement (S04)'. Re-reading S04 in full shows it publishes 46 rows under '(a) Bounty Events' (Prime, Prime Video, Audible, Kindle Unlimited, Amazon Music, registries, EBT, Amazon Business, Amazon Kids+, Prime Gaming, Amazon Haul and six Subscribe & Save rows) and a further 2 rows under '(b) Bonus Events'. The nine rows that were published were individually correct and correctly sourced — the defect was omission, not error, but a partial list carrying a completeness claim reads as the whole set.
flags.impact: A revenue model that can see only 9 of 48 special-income events systematically under-prices the non-product revenue a site can earn. Audible ($20.00) and Amazon Business ($15.00) are the two largest published bounty rates and neither was on the page.
flags.action_required: None open. ledger/commission_table.json now holds all 46 bounty rows and a new 'bonus_events' block with the 2 bonus rows; pages/commissions.html renders both and states the counts. Applied by tools/apply_bounty_completion_2026_11_14.py.

flags.title: The zero-rate caption said 'Nine category groups publish a 0.00% Standard Commission rate', which matches no grouping in the source
flags.detail: Found 2026-11-14 by session d3ce1c29. Table 1 of S04 publishes eleven bands, of which exactly two are 0.00%: the exclusion block and Coach, which Amazon lists on its own row. 'Nine' corresponds to no count in the source — eight semicolon-separated groups in the exclusion block plus Coach is the closest reading, but that count depends on how the final group ('Amazon Appstore, Prime Now, or Amazon Pay Places') is split.
flags.impact: A reader checking the claim against Table 1 cannot reconcile it, which undermines trust in the rows that are correct.
flags.action_required: None open. The caption now names the two 0.00% bands and lists what is in the exclusion block.

flags.title: tools/validate_data.py skipped any ledger row whose only source field is 'source_id' (singular)
flags.detail: Found 2026-11-14 by session d3ce1c29. check_rows() walks the ledger and yields a dict as a row only if it contains 'source_ids' or 'id'. Every commission-table row (bands, bounty rows, bonus rows, statement terms) uses the singular 'source_id' and has no 'id', so those rows were never counted and never held to the 'a row that carries a value must carry a source' rule. Completing the bounty table added 48 unchecked rows before the gap was closed.
flags.impact: The gate could not fail on an unsourced rate row — precisely the failure mode F-29 was.
flags.action_required: None open. _walk_rows now also yields on 'source_id'; the gate's row count rose from 173 to 243 and passes. Negative check: reverting the one-line change lowers the count back to 173, so the new rows are really being walked.

flags.title: The Flagged for Review panel called all 29 register items 'open items' when 17 of them are already resolved
flags.detail: Found 2026-11-14 by session d3ce1c29. pages/flags.html rendered the register under the heading 'N open items', where N was every flag in the register. At that point 5 flags carried status=closed and a further 12 had owner=done, so only 12 were genuinely awaiting the owner. The heading is the same class of defect as F-17 and F-26 — a count that does not describe the register — but in the opposite direction: it tells the reader the register is dirtier than it is.
flags.impact: An overstated open count is less dangerous than an understated one, but it is still wrong, and it buries the 12 items that really do need the owner's action inside a list that looks uniformly blocked.
flags.action_required: None open. The panel now reads 'N flagged items · X open · Y resolved', with the open count derived from status/owner by tools/build_site.py::_open_flag_count, so it cannot be typed wrong.

flags.title: Commit d6ec452 deleted 1,831 lines of COORDINATION.md — the whole session registry and task board (T1…T26)
flags.detail: Found 2026-11-14 by session d3ce1c29 while merging `main`. Commit `d6ec452` ("coordination: claim T27 for session ba8b2d38 (independent close-out)") reduced COORDINATION.md from 204,283 bytes to 43,819 bytes: `1 file changed, 51 insertions(+), 1831 deletions(-)`. The deleted block is the file header, the **session registry** for every session that has worked on this repository (6b8bb130, 6602723a, 34836ddd, ec67c431, 78c94859, f786c0d7, dc52402c, dc15ce5a, bbe4ca47, 82a2d436, 83194da0, 4338f55e, dd87f326, cdfaeefe and others) and the **task board T1 … T26** with each task's status, owner and file scope. Only the trailing session records survived. The commit message records no intent to rotate or archive the board, and `git ls-tree origin/main` shows no archive file was added, so this is recorded as an accident rather than a decision. The loss is not in the published site — no page renders COORDINATION.md — but the board is the mechanism this brief specifies for keeping parallel sessions from duplicating or colliding, and 160 KB of it was gone for the whole of the T27 close-out.
flags.impact: Without the registry and the board, a session cannot tell which task another session owns or which files are in its scope. That is precisely why flag ids collided three times in one day (F-20/F-21, F-22, then F-27/F-28 and S36/V-51…V-62 during this session's merge).
flags.action_required: Restored in this session: the board is rebuilt from `2577b70` (the last commit that still carried it) and every line that `d6ec452`…`817b6bb` added on top is re-appended, verified by a line-set check that reports **0 lines unique to main not carried over**. Owner: confirm the restored board is the version you want, and archive the log to a dated file (for example `docs/coordination/`) if it grows again rather than truncating it in place. `tools/validate_data.py::check_ledger_ids_unique` now fails the build on a duplicate ledger id, which removes the worst consequence of a lost claim.
